canonical.title: Triangle
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/3. 2D DP/05. Minimum Path in Triangle.cpp

narrative.title: The Escalator Descent Lattice
narrative.scenario: A terminal's wayfinding map is a triangular lattice of moving walkways: the apex sits at the top, and each walkway descends to one of two adjacent nodes on the row below. Every walkway posts a queue-time toll. Operations wants the least-cost descent from apex to bottom row, so the kiosk must evaluate the toll-minimal chain before suggesting a route.
narrative.inputFormat: A list triangle of rows, where row i has i+1 integers and triangle[i][j] is the toll at that node.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the minimum sum of tolls over a top-to-bottom chain of adjacent nodes.

testCases.explanation: A one-row triangle's best chain is its only node.

hintLevels: Level 1: From node (i, j) the only descendants are (i+1, j) and (i+1, j+1) — pick the cheaper.
Level 2: Sweep the rows bottom-up so each node collapses into best[i][j] = tri[i][j] + min of its two children.
Level 3: A single 1D array works because row i+1 is fully consumed before row i overwrites it; the answer is slot 0.
